title: 2011 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: On Halloween Casper ate \(\frac{1}{3}\) of his candies and then gave \(2\) candies to his brother. The next day he ate \(\frac{1}{3}\) of his remaining candies and then gave \(4\) candies to his sister. On the third day he ate his final \(8\) candies. How many candies did Casper have at the beginning?

solutions.text:
Work backward. Before giving \(4\) candies to his sister, Casper had \(12\) candies, because he ended the second day with \(8\).

Those \(12\) candies were \(\dfrac23\) of what he had after the first day, so after the first day he had \(18\) candies.

Before giving \(2\) candies to his brother, he had \(20\) candies. This was \(\dfrac23\) of his original amount, so he began with \(30\) candies.

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Work backward from the final \(8\) candies
Before giving away \(4\), Casper had \(12\), which was two thirds of the previous amount
